sections.headline: This is a place to put down roots.
sections.content: *Not just a home — a commitment to land, community, and a way of life.*

sections.headline: More than a place to live
sections.content:
Becoming a resident at Essência means becoming a member of the cooperative — an important co-steward of the land. You're not renting; you're joining a living project, with real ownership, shared governance, and legal agreements that protect you and the community alike.

This is a commitment to self-reflection, self-discovery, healing and growing proactively. Residents can be full-time or part-time depending on their life situation — you can build your own home here, raise your children, grow a business, or keep work outside, as long as you show up for the community and your commitments. Every resident contributes a few hours a week to shared life; families and our ecovillage's maintenance needs are supported with flexibility.

This is a long-term commitment — and it can also end. If the time comes to move on, the cooperative structure ensures a fair, legally supported exit process.

sections.headline: Who thrives here
sections.content: Essência is not for everyone — and that's by design. The people who thrive here are ready to live by shared values, contribute to shared life, and do the inner work that community living asks of you: physically, emotionally, mentally, energetically, and spiritually.

cards.content:
#### Live the values

Honest communication, non-harm, radical ownership, the heart path — not as rules, but as a daily practice.

#### Show up for community

A few hours of shared work each week — tending the land, cooking, building, holding space. Families are supported with flexibility.

#### Full-time or part-time

Residency adapts to your life. Keep a job, build a business, travel — as long as you remain connected and committed.

#### Long-term intention

We're building something for generations. We look for people ready to invest in a place, not just pass through it.

Reimbursed within 1 year of your request, after a minimum 3-year hold. The full budget is reviewed and adopted together each year at General Assembly.

---

You choose the structure you build — yurt, tiny house, tent, dome, or clay house — in coordination with the cooperative's guidelines, and may rent it out when you're away. Full financial details and legal documents are shared once we've had a first conversation and confirmed mutual interest.

steps.title: Reach out
steps.description: Write to us. We'll send an application form and, if it's a fit, schedule a short intro call.

steps.title: Visit the land
steps.description: Come and feel it — as a guest or volunteer. At least 3 weeks recommended; most take 3 months to decide.

steps.title: Letter of intent
steps.description: If it feels right on both sides, we begin the formal process together.

steps.title: Welcome home
steps.description: Sign, join the cooperative, and start building your life here.

sections.headline: Start the conversation
sections.content: No commitment, no pressure — just a first hello. We read every message personally.
